reports.title: US Venture Capital Outlook: Midyear Update
content:
Tariffs shifted market outlook, but by how much?

As 2025 unfolds, the VC landscape is evolving in unexpected ways. While early-year optimism pointed to a rebound in liquidity and a revitalized IPO market, global tariff tensions have reshaped the narrative. IPO activity has slowed, but resilience is emerging in new forms.

Despite headwinds, six US companies have achieved billion-dollar valuations through successful listings, proving that strategic execution can still yield strong outcomes. Meanwhile, M&A activity is thriving, with VC-backed companies—especially AI-driven startups—leading 36% of all acquisitions in a record high. This signals a shift in power dynamics, where innovation-rich firms are becoming market makers.

The second half of 2025 will be pivotal. Can the momentum in secondaries and selective large exits sustain investor confidence? At this inflection point, adaptability and strategic foresight will define the winners in a constrained but opportunity-rich market.

content:

Appetite for real assets funds remains robust

With a few major closes in Q1 2025, 18 real assets funds raised $52 billion. That is roughly half of what they raised in the entirety of 2024. While the asset class is unlikely to keep up this momentum throughout the rest of the year, there are reasons for optimism around an enduring allocator appetite for infrastructure funds. The three secular trends of decarbonization, digitalization, and deglobalization continue to drive interest in the space, even amid the persistent and intensifying economic and geopolitical uncertainty.

This report spotlights our 2029 real assets AUM forecast and contains updated data on energy transition and digital infrastructure fundraising, North American and European infrastructure performance, and oil & gas dealmaking activity.

reports.title: Enterprise SaaS M&A Review
content:
PitchBook clients can access this report's Excel data pack via the Research Center on the PitchBook Platform.

Enterprise SaaS M&A sustains momentum, although market challenges weigh on valuations

The enterprise SaaS M&A sector experienced a notable resurgence in deal activity in Q1 2025, maintaining its volume with approximately 210 transactions, closely matching the high activity of Q4 2024 and significantly surpassing the 165 deals seen in Q1 2024. This robust recovery signals renewed confidence from PE firms, even as strategic acquirers refrained from large deals amid persistent economic uncertainty and greater regulatory scrutiny globally, particularly from the US.

Despite this recovery in volume, the overall value of SaaS transactions dropped by nearly 25% QoQ, down to $29.1 billion from $38.7 billion in Q4 2024. The market continues to grapple with valuation pressures stemming from interest rate volatility, regulatory pressures, and broader economic concerns around inflation and geopolitical factors. These headwinds resulted in cautious deal structuring and moderated valuations across many transaction segments.

Several high-profile megadeals drove significant portions of the quarter’s total value, including Clearlake Capital’s $5.3 billion acquisition of Modernizing Medicine, Cotiviti’s $3.1 billion buyout of Edifecs, and ServiceNow’s $2.9 billion acquisition of Moveworks. These sizable deals underscore the selective appetite for premium SaaS companies capable of strategic integration and immediate value addition.

reports.title: Gaming VC Trends
content:
Fill out the form to download a preview of this report. The full report and its Excel data pack are available through the PitchBook Platform.

Gaming VC navigates new equilibrium amid early-stage pullback and advertising tech bets

After several quarters of correction, Q1 2025 showed that gaming VC activity has stabilized—albeit at lower levels. Total venture funding dipped 3% QoQ to $1.2 billion across 134 deals, marking the lowest deal count since mid-2019. Early-stage investments continued to shrink, while late-stage and venture growth rounds gained share, fueled by fresh capital from new funds including those of Play Ventures and Laton Ventures. Despite the dry powder, investor confidence remains fragile as the market grapples with a dearth of breakout hits from prior cycles.

Major developments from Q1 2025 included Nintendo’s delay of the highly anticipated Switch 2 amid tariff turbulence, a muted M&A and exit environment, and an accelerating shift toward monetization innovation. Investment surged into backend gaming infrastructure and AI-powered platforms, with standout deals like Bria’s $40 million Series B and Beamable’s $13.5 million Series A. Meanwhile, leading platforms like Roblox and Discord doubled down on in-game advertising strategies, signaling a potential advertising tech renaissance in a segment historically resistant to standardization and programmatic scale.

Explore the full report for insights into sector bifurcation, strategic responses to macroeconomic headwinds, and which segments show resilience in the face of disruption.

The new exit playbook: How APAC’s IPO market is being rebuilt

APAC’s IPO markets are entering a new era—one that is narrower and more selective but far from closed. In this analyst note, we examine how public listings have evolved from a default exit path to a strategic liquidity tool in Asia-Pacific’s private capital markets. From India’s surge in VC-backed IPOs to China’s policy-driven constraints and Southeast Asia’s persistent scalability gaps, we explore which countries and sectors are still supporting meaningful exits. Backed by PitchBook’s IPO Predictor, we also identify where the next wave of listings is likely to come from and what it will take to succeed in a fundamentals-first public market environment.

reports.title: Europe Equity Market Outlook: Q4 2023
content: Central banks have their work cut out for them. Core inflation remains high and the sticky nature of this type of inflation means that progress in getting inflation back down to the 2% target could take significant time. This poses serious questions for central banks: keep rates high and risk a recession, or reduce rates and potentially have to deal with an overheating economy?

reports.title: North America Market Outlook: Q4 2023
content: According to a composite of the over 700 stocks we cover that trade on U.S. exchanges, as of Sept. 25, 2023, the U.S. equity market was trading at a price/fair value of 0.92, representing an 8% discount to our fair value estimates. Upward momentum propelled the market higher in July, and our price/fair value metric briefly touched fair value before the market gave up those gains and then some. Hawkish commentary from the U.S. Federal Reserve, rising energy prices, and higher interest rates took their toll in August and September.

reports.title: Interest-Rate Risk Factor Swamps Bank Stock Valuations
content: While company-specific results have seemed to matter during earnings, improved valuations for banks have had a hard time holding up over time. Why is this? We believe an interest-rate risk factor is overriding most idiosyncratic factors for now. The first risk is the potential for higher short-term rates.

reports.title: PitchBook Analyst Note: VC Investment in Climate Tech
content:
Note: This is the free edition of premium content produced by our Industry and Technology Research team. As a result, parts of this version are blurred out. The full version is available only to PitchBook clients.

VC investment in climate tech falls for the third year in a row

Venture capital investment in climate tech continued its downward trend in Q1 2025, with deal value holding steady at $9 billion following a trend of steadily decreasing annual deal value since the sector’s peak in 2021. Despite the overall slowdown in dealmaking, the quarter was marked by strong deal value for dispatchable energy sources such as nuclear and geothermal energy as well as industrial decarbonization technologies.

The impacts of tariffs and supply chain challenges remain key for investors and VC-backed companies in the climate tech space, particularly for US-based companies. In addition to deal activity, this analyst note explores how AI is reshaping climate tech—including applications for optimizing battery performance and interpreting complex datasets in order to monitor large areas of land.

reports.title: US Private Equity Outlook: Midyear Update
content:
PitchBook clients can access this report's Excel data pack via the Research Center on the PitchBook Platform.

US PE adapts amid a fuzzier outlook

The US private equity ecosystem entered 2025 with strong momentum that was halted by broad market uncertainty at the beginning of Q2. PE is now tasked with balancing these new market headwinds with its desire to reignite this momentum. Despite the hiccups, IPO activity for PE has gotten off to a healthy start this year. However, the challenge is whether the IPO window will remain open for PE-backed companies. Similarly, the recent market slowdown will likely stall overall exit activity, seeing sponsors hold on to portfolio companies for longer, further limiting distributions to LPs and hampering fundraising activity in the back half of the year.

Trade-tariff volatility impacts EMEA private markets

As we reach the midyear mark, our analysts revisit their 2025 forecasts in light of recent developments. Trade tariffs have introduced unexpected volatility so far this year, impacting private markets. This follow-up note provides an updated perspective on key trends, including PE middle-market fundraising, GP-leds, venture debt, IPOs, AI, and Middle East & North Africa fundraising.
